WASHINGTON (AP) — A battle over abortion rights is playing out in several states Tuesday as voters decide 145 proposed laws and constitutional amendments, including some that could affect voting for future elections.

The ballot measures provide a political undercard for a high-profile midterm election that will determine which party controls Congress, state legislatures and gubernatorial offices in many states.

Stand with free and independent journalism. Join Press Pass from PBS News

Some measures put President Donald Trump's priorities to a public test by gauging support for his attempts to reshape congressional districts, limit transgender athletes in sports and strengthen voter identification requirements.

Two years ago, Missouri voters became the first in the nation to pass a ballot measure undoing an existing ban on most abortions.

Now voters are deciding whether to repeal the 2024 abortion rights amendment and replace it with a new prohibition — this time allowing exceptions for medical emergencies and fetal anomalies, and in cases of rape or incest up to 12 weeks of pregnancy. The proposed ban was placed on the ballot by the Republican-led Legislature. Abortion rights advocates, led by national progressive groups, have greatly outspent abortion foes in a bid to defeat the measure.

national.title: Bomb threats target seven flights across Europe
national.summary: Planes in Poland, Spain, Bulgaria and Italy have been checked for explosives following separate threats.
national.body:
Seven passenger planes across Europe, two of which departed from the UK, have been inspected following a series of suspected bomb threats.

Two Ryanair flights, one originating from Dublin and the other from Lisbon, were searched after landing in Rome following anonymous tips but no explosives were found, sources at the city's Fiumicino airport told the BBC.

The Dublin flight was escorted by the Italian air force until landing.

Authorities have also searched planes in Poland, Spain and Bulgaria.

It is unclear if the incidents are connected. While officially there is no link between them, authorities from various countries will be co-operating to assess whether this was a co-ordinated attack, designed to disrupt airspace.

The UK government described today's incidents as "malicious hoax threats".

In a statement it said it had "one of the most robust aviation security systems in the world, with well-tested processes for dealing with any potential threats, as well as malicious hoax threats, like those we've seen today".

Aviation security expert Paul Mason said bomb threats on passenger planes "don't happen that frequently", which made the latest incidents "unusual".

national.body: The majority state-owned Saudi Aramco, the largest oil company in the world, on Tuesday reported a 35% increase in third-quarter net profit as earnings were boosted by higher oil prices and the sale of its stake in a Malaysian refining and petrochemical company. Net profit rose to $36.3 billion from $26.9 billion in the year-earlier quarter. Adjusted net profit, which leaves out the sale of a stake in PRefChem to Malaysian state oil company Petronas, rose 9% to $31.2 billion. The company also benefitted from high profit margins at its refineries turning crude into usable products such as diesel fuel. Saudi Aramco sold its oil for an average of $95.20 a barrel during the quarter, compared to $70.10 in the year-before quarter, the company said in a news release. Oil prices surged after the outbreak of the Iran war due to disruption of supply and uncertainty about the course of the conflict. After the war began, Saudi Aramco was able to use its East-West pipeline to the Red Sea port of Yanbu to maintain a significant share of its oil exports despite disruption of tanker traffic through the Strait of Hormuz due to the risk of Iranian attack. The pipeline was attacked Sept. 10 but has since resumed flows. Saudi oil is now also being transported through the strait using a U.S.-protected corridor near the coast of Oman. Exports have continued despite attacks on Aramco facilities by Iranian-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen. AP/CBS

national.title: Irish Olympian Ciara Mageean was a 'talented and inspirational human being'
national.summary: The former European champion and two-time Olympic runner had been diagnosed with stage four bowel cancer.
national.body:
Olympian Ciara Mageean has been described as a "truly remarkable, immensely talented and inspirational human being" in a tribute read out at her funeral.

Hundreds of people have paid their respects to the runner at her funeral on Tuesday.

The former European champion and two-time Olympic runner died on Sunday after she was diagnosed with stage four bowel cancer.

Among those in attendance at the funeral in Portaferry, County Down, were Northern Ireland First Minister Michelle O'Neill, as well as fellow Olympian Rhys McClenaghan and 1972 gold medallist Lady Mary Peters.

Mageean's funeral cortege was given a guard of honour by Portaferry GAC and her former school, Assumption Grammar in Ballynahinch.

Her death comes less than three weeks after her marriage to her long-term partner Thomas Moran.

Mourners began arriving at around midday for the 2:00 GMT requiem Mass at St Patrick's Church.

Family, friends and those wishing to pay their respects followed the funeral cortege the short distance along the Ballyphilip Road from Mageean's family home to the church.

national.summary: Proposition 40 would impose a one-time 5% tax on the wealth of Californians whose net worth exceeds $1 billion, with most of the revenue dedicated to replacing federal funding cuts to healthcare.

SACRAMENTO, Calif. (AP) — California could become the first state in the nation to tax the net worth of billionaires Tuesday under a ballot measure that has divided liberal leaders nationally and triggered one of the most expensive ballot fights in state history as the ultra-rich scramble to figure out whether they would pay the tax or flee.

Proposition 40 would impose a one-time 5% tax on the wealth of Californians whose net worth exceeds $1 billion, with most of the revenue dedicated to replacing federal funding cuts to healthcare.

Vermont Sen. Bernie Sanders has framed the proposal as a monumental step toward reining in deep wealth inequality by ensuring the ultra-rich pay their fair share. But Democratic Gov. Gavin Newsom warns it would prompt the state's wealthiest to move out of California and take their tax money with them.

Stand with free and independent journalism. Join Press Pass from PBS News

The "no" side has raised roughly 10 times as much as the "yes" side, thanks in large part to tech moguls and venture capitalists, who have poured millions into a political action committee fighting the measure. Billionaires are already bracing for its approval. Some of them, including Google co-founders Sergey Brin and Larry Page, started cutting ties with the state after the measure was unveiled. Mark Zuckerberg said he would stay in California for eight years and made a deal with Meta that would help him pay the tax without losing his ownership stake in the company.

Backers of the proposed tax, led by the powerful labor union SEIU United Healthcare Workers West, say it's needed to help the state backfill the federal funding cuts. The union estimates the state will lose $100 billion in federal healthcare funding over five years.

national.title: Death toll rises in Ukraine after Russia attacks aid centre, hospice and hospital
national.summary: At least 38 people are killed in 24 hours and Ukraine's Volodymyr Zelensky warns dozens more could be trapped under rubble.
national.body:
Russian strikes on Ukraine – including on an aid centre, a hospice and a hospital – have killed at least 38 civilians and injured scores of others across Ukraine over the last 24 hours.

At least 33 people are known to have died in a glide bomb attack in the southern Zaporizhzhia region on Monday night, and President Volodymyr Zelensky said the number of victims was set to rise as more than 50 people could be trapped under the rubble.

He called the strike in Komyshuvakha village "one of the largest mass killings committed by Russia during this war".

Ukraine had proposed to extend and expand last week's ceasefire in the Kherson region which allowed people from the frontline Russian-occupied town of Oleshky to evacuate, Zelensky added.

The attack on a school building being used as an aid distribution centre in Komyshuvakha was Moscow's response, he said.

Elsewhere, a hospice was attacked in the central city of Dnipro and a hospital was hit in the north-eastern city of Kharkiv, where Zelensky said 73 people were wounded, most of them elderly patients.

Nine 3,000kg aerial bombs hit Komyshuvakha as residents were gathering to receive humanitarian aid at a distribution centre, authorities said. Local media reported that when the attack began, people took refuge underground but the roof collapsed, trapping many underneath.

"The scale of the tragedy is difficult to comprehend," regional head Mykhailo Semikin said.

HARRISBURG, Pa. (AP) — Democrats are heading into Tuesday's midterm elections hoping to take over a majority of governors' offices for the first time in two decades, as they ride a wave of voter discontent over the economy, inflation, healthcare and the future of democracy.

The number of states in play is surprisingly large, a reflection of President Donald Trump's poor approval ratings dragging on his party. Competitive races include those in heavily populated states such as Texas and Florida; presidential battleground states such as Michigan and Wisconsin; and reliably red states such as Iowa and Ohio.

In the weeks leading up to Election Day, Trump went to heavily Republican areas to headline rallies attended by GOP gubernatorial candidates looking for a boost.

Stand with free and independent journalism. Join Press Pass from PBS News

All told, 36 states that are home to about 80% of the nation's population will elect a governor Tuesday. In 19 states, the office is open. Heading into the elections, Democratic governors represented 60% of the nation's population, but Republicans held 26 of the nation's 50 governors' offices.

"Our goal is not just the majority of the population, but the majority of states," Meghan Meehan-Draper, the executive director of the Democratic Governors Association, told The Associated Press.

Democrats last gained a majority of governorships in 2006, flipping six governors' offices in the last midterm under a second-term Republican president. Republicans recaptured the majority four years later.

Most U.S. voters who are deciding Senate races Tuesday will pick one candidate. For voters in Alaska and Maine, their ballots instead will offer the chance to rank candidates in what is known as ranked choice voting.

Maine and Alaska are the only two states using the voting method to select a U.S. senator this election. Those competitive races, ranked as "toss ups" by the Cook Political Report with Amy Walter , are seen as key to which party controls Congress.

"Ranked choice voting has a few different goals," said Derek Tisler, elections expert for the Brennan Center for Justice. "One is to ensure that the ultimate winner reflects majority support, and two is to allow voters to support more candidates without worrying that their vote is going to be wasted."

WATCH: How open primaries and ranked choice voting can help break partisan gridlock

Ranked choice voting itself doesn't lead to later election results, experts told PBS News, but it can be a factor. When polls close Tuesday in Alaska and Maine, it may take some time for news outlets to report a winner. For these two close Senate races, newsrooms that make projections may need more of the official results than they do for other contests before they can confidently predict the winner.

PBS News relies on race calls from The Associated Press to report the winners before election officials certify the results. Official election results take weeks as every vote is counted and certified.

WASHINGTON (AP) — The stakes in Tuesday's election — which party will control Congress — are crystal clear. But when that will be known is impossible to say.

The Associated Press will be calling races in all 435 House districts and the 35 Senate contests that are up for election this year.

Control of the House depends on which party reaches 218 seats. Currently, 219 members caucus with Republicans, just one more than the minimum needed for a majority when all seats are filled. There are two vacancies now.

Stand with free and independent journalism. Join Press Pass from PBS News

The bar for the Senate is 51 seats for Democrats or 50 for Republicans, since Vice President JD Vance can cast a tiebreaking vote for his party. Republicans have a 53-47 edge in the Senate right now.

During the last midterm elections in 2022, the AP called control of the Senate four days after Election Day, while the House call was eight days after.

national.summary: If Republicans lose control of Congress, the rest of his time in office is likely to be consumed by Democratic-led investigations into his administration and his business dealings, and possibly even another impeachment.

WASHINGTON (AP) — For Donald Trump, Tuesday's elections will chart the course for the final two years of his presidency.

If his party loses control of Congress in the midterm elections, the rest of his time in office is likely to be consumed by Democratic-led investigations into his administration and his business dealings, and possibly even another impeachment. The political spotlight will also begin its shift to Republicans and Democrats vying to replace him during the 2028 presidential campaign.

Stand with free and independent journalism. Join Press Pass from PBS News

Beyond that, if voters deliver a rebuke to Republicans on Tuesday, Trump will be left with dramatically diminished political capital at home and abroad, as he has all but guaranteed the results will be seen as a referendum on himself by repeatedly urging voters to "pretend I'm on the ballot."

Placing himself front and center on voters' minds was a major gamble by the president and his political team, who believed personalizing the midterms would activate "Make America Great Again" supporters who might otherwise be less likely to turn out when Trump was not an official candidate. Democrats were eager to watch the unpopular president insert himself so fully in the campaign, believing it's served as an effective reminder of who should be blamed for the state of the economy, which voters said was their top concern.

national.title: Rain moves out as flood risks remain in Southwest following destructive storms
national.summary: An expert says over 20 trillion gallons of water has fallen on the Four Corners states and Nevada in the past two weeks. The flooding has kept swift-water rescue teams busy.
national.body:
Christopher Weber, Associated Press Christopher Weber, Associated Press

The skies were clearing, but the risk of flooding remained over parts of the U.S. Southwest after powerful downpours sent massive amounts of water surging over the usually dry landscape, forcing hundreds to evacuate and keeping swift-water rescue teams busy.

Officials said cleanup and repair efforts could take weeks. One person died in the floodwaters and police suspect a second death was weather-related.

The National Weather Service said Monday that isolated cloudbursts were still possible across the Four Corners region — where New Mexico, Arizona, Colorado and Utah meet — as the phenomenon stoked by warming Pacific waters known as El Niño disrupts weather patterns.

Damage was widespread in Pagosa Springs, Colorado, a town of about 2,000. Officials feared the San Juan River that flows through it would top a level that nearly wiped out the town in 1911. The river reached 16.81 feet (5.1 meters) Sunday — a foot lower than the historic level — flooding downtown streets before receding Monday, the weather service said.

An entire home was lifted from its foundation and floated down the river before crashing into a pedestrian bridge. A section of a road bridge west of town crumbled under raging waters, said Archuleta County Sheriff's Office spokesperson Vicki Shaffer.

Dozens of people were rescued across the region, including some by helicopter. Shaffer said first responders were searching for people who may be stranded.

national.title: Binance says fake job interviews used as part of $6.3bn crypto hack
national.summary: An engineer was contacted through a legitimate job-hunting platform and invited to bogus job interviews with fake company representatives, Binance says.
national.body:
Hackers who stole a record $6.3bn (£4.7bn) from Binance used fake job interviews and a compromised internal AI tool, the firm has revealed.

Initial findings published by the company, which operates the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, said hackers gained access to its systems through "sophisticated, multi-stage campaign".

It said they used a range of techniques such as malicious software downloads to compromise the computers of Binance engineers and gain control over tools to drain its wallet of billions of dollars worth of crypto.

Binance called it a "serious and highly sophisticated security incident" and apologised, saying "this should not have happened".

In a post on X , external , Binance said hackers targeted its engineers using social engineering techniques.

These see hackers use approaches such as phishing to trick people into parting with sensitive or personal details, that can then be used to try and access their accounts.

Binance said as part of the hack, one of its engineers was contacted through a legitimate job-hunting platform and invited to bogus job interviews with fake company representatives.

It said the perpetrators used "more advanced and deceptive" methods to build trust with him, such as sharing social media accounts that contained personal images.

national.title: A new HIV-prevention drug is showing promising signs, but it's difficult to find in Africa and beyond
national.summary: Demand for lenacapavir is far outstripping supply in Uganda, other parts of Africa and all over the world. U.S. regulators on Monday approved a generic version for sale in low-income countries.
national.body:
MBARARA, Uganda (AP) — In the red light district in Mbarara, a city in western Uganda known in part for sex tourism, a sex worker named Lisa Mutoni insists on using condoms when men enter her room, to protect her against HIV and other infections. The problem: Some try to remove or tear the condom while having sex.

She takes HIV-prevention medication called PrEP, or preexposure prophylaxis, which can come in the form of daily pills or periodic injections. But there's a new option for her and millions like her — if they could only get it. It's a drug called lenacapavir that studies have shown can offer nearly complete protection from HIV with just two shots a year.

Mutoni said access to lenacapavir would benefit sex workers who sometimes shift elsewhere for months at a time.

"If you know that you have that injection for six months, you feel like you are safe," she said. "And then it is very good, nice because sometimes you can also forget, if it is the pill, you can forget to swallow."

But Mutoni says every time she tries to get what is commonly referred to as "lena," it's not available. "They tell me that it is finished," she said.

Such is the promise and the frustration with lenacapavir, a drug developed by Gilead Sciences. Other PrEP options, including pills and an every-other-month shot of the drug cabotegravir, are very effective and widely available. But health experts say lenacapavir has the power not just to protect individuals but potentially even turn the tide of the HIV epidemic globally because of its long-lasting effects.

A health official administers Lenacapavir, a long‑acting HIV prevention injection, in Epworth outside the capital Harare, Zimbabwe, February 19, 2026.Photo by Philimon Bulawayo/Reuters.

But there are not nearly enough doses, in this East African country or the rest of the world.

KYIV, Ukraine (AP) — Rescuers in southern Ukraine continued an intense search Tuesday for survivors at a bombed-out aid facility and shelter where at least 31 people were killed and dozens were still missing.

As Ukraine prepared for a new round of U.S.-brokered peace negotiations next week, a wave of overnight strikes targeted power plants across the country, damaged hospitals and wounded scores of people.

The United States launched strikes on Iranian targets, a U.S. official said, in what appeared to be a limited operation on the eve of Tuesday's crucial midterm elections.

Iranian state media reported explosions being heard on the islands of Qeshm and Hengam in the strategic Strait of Hormuz, and in the nearby mainland area of Bandar Abbas. Unlike earlier in the war, the strikes were not publicly announced.

national.title: Mining giant joins fight to stop killer toad march across Australia
national.summary: Rio Tinto is jointly funding a A$28m "toad containment zoe" to protect the Pilbara region.
national.body:
Rio Tinto is ploughing millions of dollars into stopping the poisonous cane toad reaching the Pilbara region of western Australia, where the mining giant has a vast iron ore operation.

The firm, alongside Curtin University in Perth and others, will spend A$28m (£14.5m) building a "toad containment zone" to prevent the pest travelling south.

While the cane toad is not a direct threat to Rio Tinto's business, it produces toxins lethal to native wildlife and poses a threat to Pilbara's ecosystem.

Rio Tinto has previously faced criticism for destroying two sacred Aboriginal rock shelters in Pilbara which sat above tonnes of iron ore.

The decision cost the former chief executive his job, provoked a widespread backlash and saw Rio Tinto commit to rebuilding trust with Indigenous communities.

Commenting on the proposed containment zone, Roberta Hunter, a ranger in Australia's Nyangumarta Warrarn Indigenous Protected Area, said: "Cane toads destroy the water and animals.

"When toads come close to our country, we want to be there to stop them because we don't want the country to be destroyed."

The plan is to cut off the toad's water supply by building a barrier across 7,500 sq km (2,895 sq m) of land between the Great Sandy Desert and the Indian Ocean.

national.body:
Lindsay Whitehurst, Associated Press Lindsay Whitehurst, Associated Press

Michael Kunzelman, Associated Press Michael Kunzelman, Associated Press

WASHINGTON (AP) — The Supreme Court will hear arguments Tuesday in a case brought by Catholic preschools that say it's unconstitutional to exclude them from a state-funded program over their admissions policy for LGBTQ+ families, the latest religious-rights case before the conservative-majority court.

Arguments begin at 10 a.m. EST. Listen live in the video player above.

Colorado says their refusal to admit kids from those families violates the state's anti-discrimination law.

But St. Mary Catholic Parish and the Archdiocese of Denver argue that the policy is based on religious teachings about same-sex marriage and that excluding them violates their free-exercise rights.

President Donald Trump's administration is supporting the Catholic institutions.

A win for the preschools could further narrow a landmark 1990 Supreme Court decision that found religious practices don't create exemptions from laws that otherwise apply broadly. Written by conservative icon Justice Antonin Scalia in a case over the spiritual use of peyote, a cactus containing mescaline that's sacred to many Indigenous people, the decision has nevertheless long been a target of the conservative legal movement.

national.title: Libya's top religious authority rules against wearing Nike clothes
national.summary: The US company was named after the Greek goddess of victory, so the Dar al-Ifta said displaying its logo was unIslamic.
national.body:
Libya's highest religious authority, the Dar al-Ifta, has issued a ruling banning Muslims from buying, selling or wearing clothing bearing the Nike logo.

The ruling, issued by the Tripoli-based institution, states that the US sportswear giant was named after the Greek goddess of victory and that its famous swoosh logo was inspired by her wings.

It argued that wearing clothing displaying the logo amounted to promoting symbols associated "with polytheism," or the worship of more than one god.

Libya is home to the ancient Greek city of Cyrene, where archaeological remains include a statue of the Greek goddess of the same name.

The religious committee also accused Nike of supporting Israel and called for a boycott of companies that back the country.

It referred to a statement issued by its Council for Research and Sharia Studies on 5 November 2023, urging Muslims to boycott Western companies it considers supportive of Israel during the war in Gaza.

The ruling, known as a fatwa, is a religious opinion on a matter of Islamic law. It was approved by Libya's Grand Mufti, Sadiq al-Gharyani.

The Dar al-Ifta is an influential religious institution based in Tripoli, in western Libya. The country is politically divided, with rival authorities and institutions operating in the east and west after years of conflict following the toppling of long-time leader Muammar Gaddafi in 2011.

"We want military spouses to know that they can and should take this time for themselves," said Benjamin Pomerance, deputy counsel for the state Department of Veterans' Services.

Pomerance and his team of wellness experts, including Stress Is Gone with Brett Cotter, are putting together this inaugural getaway as an extension of the Healing Haven for Military Spouses virtual program.

The program, which started in December 2025, Pomerance said offers a safe space where military spouses can "gather in community with each other in a professionally facilitated manner"

"When someone is serving in military uniform, that entire family is serving with them," Pomerance said. "There's just something powerful of being in community with people who have had experiences that are similar to yours, who can talk the same language, so to speak."

Military spouses play a vital yet often undervalued role in supporting those who serve, officials said. Loved ones must navigate deployments, frequent uprooting, adjusting to a one-parent household, and supporting partners who are transitioning back to civilian life.

"The challenges in some ways can be just as great after they come back home and everybody's dealing with the newness of that experience," said Laura Heltz, executive director of the Veterans Outreach Center in Rochester. "A lot of times the service member wants to sort of shield the spouse from some of those issues."

Patricia M. (Danforth) Babcock, 82, of Fredonia, passed away Sunday morning, November 1, 2026 at the Chautauqua Nursing and Rehab Center. She was born in Dunkirk on December 31, 1943, she was the wife of Robert R. Babcock II, and daughter of the late Byron and Bernice (Kraiger) Danforth.

A lifelong resident of Dunkirk and Fredonia, Patricia graduated from Dunkirk High School.

Patricia was a loving wife, and mother who devoted much of her life to caring for her family. Over the years, she worked in food service, including positions in the cafeteria at Niagara Mohawk and at the Bomber House. She also took great pride in her role as a homemaker.

Patricia enjoyed working with ceramics and spending time tending to her flower garden. She was an active member of St. John's Church, where she enjoyed being involved in her church community. Patricia will be remembered for her love and devotion to her family and the care she showed to those around her.

Patricia is survived by her loving husband of 56 years, Robert Babcock II, her sons, Sean Morrison, John (Jami) Babcock, Patrick (Margaret) Babcock, Robert (Michelle) Babcock III, and Steven Babcock; five grandchildren and her siblings, John (Lori) Danforth and Barbara Adamczak.

In addition to her parents, she is preceded in death by her grandson, Jared Babcock.

Relatives and friends are welcome to attend Calling Hours on Wednesday, November 4, 2026 from 2-4 p.m. and 6-8 p.m. at the McGraw-Kowal Funeral Home, 736 Central Avenue, Dunkirk, NY. Prayer services will begin at 6 p.m. Interment will be held privately in Willowbrook Park Cemetery. Arrangements are by R. Michael Mackowiak III; McGraw-Kowal Funeral Home. Share condolences at, www.mcgrawkowalfuneralhome.com.

local.body:
The newest edition of a plan to revamp Wright Park Beach and Lakefront Boulevard moves the beach slightly west and keeps the road open.

The city of Dunkirk Planning and Development Department held a joint online meeting with the Buffalo Niagara Waterkeeper organization Tuesday to describe the latest plan.

"This has been a fantastic project that has helped some of the best coastal engineers of the country look at Wright Park and Lakefront Boulevard as a system," city Planning and Development Director Vince DeJoy said.

"It’s been a fabulous team effort and it doesn't end here," he said. The plan discussed Tuesday "represents 30% (of the) design and engineering" for the improvement project. "We have submitted a grant application to get to a full design and engineering, to allow us to then apply for grant funding for implementation," he said.

DeJoy noted that he will be moving to North Carolina shortly, but talked up his deputy director EJ Hayes, stating that Hayes should be able to fill his shoes seamlessly on the project.

The presentation listed the following big-picture objectives for the project:

-- Emphasize nature-based strategies, habitat preservation and creation.

-- Protect critical infrastructure along Lakefront Boulevard, along with the nearby wastewater treatment plant.

local.body:
OBSERVER Photo by Braden Carmen Fredonia seniors Elly Saunders (1) and Londyn Wilmot (8) celebrate with Alyse Bugaj (7) and their teammates after a point during Monday’s Section VI Class B2 semifinal girls volleyball game against Springville Griffith at Fredonia High School.

OBSERVER Photo by Braden Carmen Fredonia libero Sophia Pagan returns a serve during a Section VI Class B2 semifinal girls volleyball game on Monday at Fredonia High School.

FREDONIA -- Two years ago, the Fredonia 'Billies were Section VI champions. This year, they will play for that honor again, and their coach believes they deserve the crown as much as any team she has ever coached.

"I haven't had a team this unified, where everyone wants this, everyone is willing to put in what it takes to get there," Fredonia head coach Amanda Krakowiak said. "It's a dream to have a team like this. They have the heart and they really, really want this. It's just amazing to work with a group of girls like that."

Fredonia claimed its spot back in the sectional title game with a victory over the Springville Griffith Griffins 25-8, 25-10, a 25-12 in Monday's Class B2 semifinal volleyball match at Fredonia High School.

"We have a really good connection. Getting these big wins like this one is really amazing, to be able to do that with everyone we've grown so close with over the years," said Fredonia senior Elly Saunders.

The 'Billies essentially brought back the same team it had a year ago. But the story of this year's team dates back to two years ago when the 'Billies won the sectional championship with a win over Southwestern, then with a win over Depew in the Class B crossover.

"One of the things I had preached to that team a couple years ago was, 'You guys are paving the path for the future, creating this opportunity for the future teams here at Fredonia. They are going to look up to you and they are going to see that this team was able to do it,'" Krakowiak said.

local.title: Portville survives Chautauqua Lake in 5 sets
local.summary: PORTVILLE — The Portville girls volleyball team has won every Section VI Class C volleyball championship since 2014 and the Panthers have claimed the last five New York State Public High School Athletic Association championships. In recent years, Portville has seldom been tested in the sectional pla
local.body:
PORTVILLE -- The Portville girls volleyball team has won every Section VI Class C volleyball championship since 2014 and the Panthers have claimed the last five New York State Public High School Athletic Association championships.

In recent years, Portville has seldom been tested in the sectional playoffs and has cruised to several of its state titles. However, with three losses in the regular season, the Panthers looked beatable to some teams in Class C.

That set the stage for the Section VI Class C semifinals on Monday with No. 1 Portville hosting No. 4 Chautauqua Lake -- which is ranked second in the state, according to the New York State Sportswriters Association -- making for a state-level competition. The undefeated Eagles showed they were right on the level of Portville with a 25-23 win in the first set, but the Panthers hung on in the back-and-forth contest that finished in five sets with the streak staying alive 23-25, 25-22, 22-25, 25-15, 15-13.

"Any time you play Portville there is a lot of hype behind it," Chautauqua Lake head coach Joanne Meadows said. "I think with the team I had this year everybody thought it would be a great match and it was a great match. I really can't ask a lot more from my kids than what they did. We had a couple of times where we made a few mistakes, but it's high school volleyball (and) there is going to be mistakes. I'm very proud of the way they played. It was an awesome match and I think it lived up to what everyone thought it was going to be."

In a rematch of last year's semifinals, Chautauqua Lake showed it was up to the task, unlike last year when the Eagles were quickly swept. Falling behind 20-15, the Eagles were not fazed by the score and seized the momentum at the end of the set with runs of four and three in a 25-23 win.

"I think it absolutely gave us a boost," Meadows said about winning the opening set. "Last year we came here and got absolutely swept and bombed. When they came in this year and took the first set that definitely increased the momentum for us for a little while. Volleyball is such a momentum sport, so that really makes a difference."

The loss was Portville's first in the Section VI playoffs since 2022 when it dropped one set against Eden in the final.

Chautauqua Lake rode that wave into the second set and jumped to a 5-1 lead that included two big kills from freshman Brina Jacobson and an ace by senior setter Karagan Fairbank.

local.body:
The Dunkirk City School District has awarded dozens of bids worth more than $21 million for the next phase of its long-term construction project.

The Dunkirk Board of Education approved the bids for Phase 1.3 of the project at its October meeting. A total of 24 bids were awarded in six areas of work.

District Superintendent Brian Swatland called it "the biggest phase" in the capital project.

The cafeteria and kitchen at the Middle and High School will get renovated. A new connecting corridor and courtyard will be added at the school. The football field, track, and tennis courts are getting refurbished, and new scoreboards are planned.

In addition, air conditioning will be added to district classrooms. Finally, a new "School Based Health Office" will get added.

The capital project already has a visible benefit: Construction is complete on a new Sixth Street entrance and addition.

local.body:
Pick a Thanksgiving table, any Thanksgiving table in America, and it’s sure to have a turkey and a grumpy uncle.

Sometimes they are one and the same, stuffed with all the trimmings.

As the midterms are decided, this November will be an especially heated month, right? We the people are so deeply carved down the center. There’s no moderate middle ground.

As the presumptive winners of the House, the Democratic family members get the white meat. The Republicans will have to do with dark. The winner of the Senate gets dibs on pumpkin pie.

Oh, what a feast it will be for starved Democrats, after two long years in the Donald Trump wilderness. It feels like 40, right?

Elon Musk, Trump’s loaded right-hand man, will gobble up leftovers at his knee like a DOGE, but he won’t have a place at the table.

Everything we love, everything we thought we knew about America, is under siege.

Under the usual circumstances, the grumpy uncle could pass with his harsh social comments, his barely disguised racism and his loud voice trumpeting over the younger company.

local.title: 'People keep dying': Second crash in 11 days at Lockport intersection
local.summary: Neighbors who live near the intersection of Bartz and Rapids roads in the Town of Lockport are calling for safety changes after two people were killed in separate crashes there last month.
local.body: Neighbors who live near the intersection of Bartz and Rapids roads in the Town of Lockport are calling for safety changes after two people were killed in separate crashes there last month.The most recent crash happened Friday and claimed the life of a 27-year-old mother of two young children.Henry Kamens has lived on Bartz Road for nearly 40 years and said he has seen crash after crash at the intersection."I don't know what they have to do," Kamens said. "People keep dying."Another fatal crash happened Oct. 19. In that case, Kamens said a Jeep stopped at the stop sign on Bartz Road and then drove into the path of a cement truck traveling on Rapids Road.At the intersection, Crosby Road becomes Bartz Road. Drivers traveling on Bartz and Crosby have a stop sign, while traffic on Rapids Road does not.Kamens believes some drivers mistakenly think the intersection is a four-way stop."They think it's a four-way stop," Kamens said. "They just look, you know.... they stop and they just go. They don't really think that the traffic is coming, even though we have signs up there."Kamens said he'd like to see additional traffic controls installed."I think they should put either a signal in or a four-way stop," he said.Town of Lockport Supervisor Mark Crocker said the NYS Department of Transportation has previously determined there was not enough traffic at the intersection to warrant a traffic signal.WATCH: 'People keep dying': Second crash in 11 days at Lockport intersectionCrocker also said Niagara County recently spent $6 million on Rapids Road, including regrading the slope of the roadway in an effort to improve visibility at the intersection.They've also put up signs ahead of the stop signs indicating that the cross traffic doesn't have a stop sign. local.title: Union Road bridge in West Seneca fully reopens after months of construction
local.summary: After months of traffic disruptions and a pause in work to protect a threatened fish species, the Union Road bridge over Cazenovia Creek in West Seneca has fully reopened.
local.body: After months of traffic disruptions and a pause in work to protect a threatened fish species, the Union Road bridge over Cazenovia Creek in West Seneca has fully reopened.The New York State Department of Transportation confirmed the bridge is now open to traffic, marking the substantial completion of a project designed to protect the structure's long-term safety and integrity.The project faced several setbacks, including structural issues, weather and environmental restrictions.Earlier this year, construction crews were unable to perform work in the creek between May 1 and June 30 because of state environmental protections for the bigeye chub, a threatened fish species found only in Western New York.At the time, the DOT said work on the bridge's substructure would resume July 1, with the overall project expected to be completed by the end of 2026.The extended construction period also frustrated nearby businesses and motorists.Now, the bridge is fully reopened, although construction crews still have some work to finish.WATCH: Union Road bridge in West Seneca fully reopens after months of constructionThe DOT says finishing work will continue through the remainder of the year, with occasional single-lane closures anticipated over the next several weeks.In a statement, the department acknowledged the disruption the project caused."The Department of Transportation recognizes the significant impact construction has had on motorists and the West Seneca community, and we appreciate the public's patience throughout construction," A NYSDOT spokesperson said.The department has not provided a specific date for when all remaining work will be completed.

entertainment.body:
Logo text Neve Campbell will return as Sidney Prescott in Scream 8.

Campbell confirmed to the Associated Press Monday night that she will reprise the role as horror’s iconic final girl for the eighth installment of the franchise. While discussing her upcoming projects, the actress revealed that she has two shows in development, one of which she has sold, in addition to “ Scream 8 — that’s in the pipeline as well.”

“I can never tell you anything about Scream 8,” she said when asked to share more. Though she added with a laugh, “I’ll be in it!” Related Stories Movies Vice Studios Taps ThankYouX as Artist in Residence Movies 'Crawl 2' Adds Sarah Niles, Ray Panthaki and 3 More Ahead of 2027 Paramount Release (Exclusive)

Campbell has been a central figure in the franchise since the original 1996 film. She starred in the first four films of Wes Craven’s series before the franchise was revamped with Scream (2022), which followed the Carpenter sisters played by Melissa Barrera and Jenna Ortega. Campbell appeared in a smaller role.

She notably sat out of Scream VI over salary disputes . Following the sixth film’s release, Barrera was fired from the franchise over her social media posts on the Israel-Hamas war. Ortega then exited the series voluntarily .

Campbell returned for Spyglass Media and Paramount Pictures ‘ Scream 7 , released in February, which centered on Sidney and her onscreen daughter Tatum (Isabel May). The film became the highest-grossing installment, earning $208 million worldwide on a $45 million budget.

A month after the film’s release, The Hollywood Reporter confirmed that Scream 8 was in development at Spyglass, with sisters Lilla and Nora Zuckerman writing the script.

entertainment.body:
Jade earns her first solo hit on the Billboard Hot 100 as her single “Angel of My Dreams” debuts at No. 70 on the chart dated Nov. 7 — more than two years after its release. She becomes the first member of Little Mix to reach the chart as a soloist. Explore Jade Thirlwall Little Mix See latest videos, charts and news

The song debuts almost entirely on the strength of streaming. It drew 3.8 million official U.S. streams (up 65%) in the Oct. 23-29 tracking week, according to Luminate. Related Justin Timberlake to Release 4-Part Docuseries That Includes Janet Jackson as a Guest Bruce Springsteen Backs Michigan's Dr. Abdul El-Sayed for U.S. Senate Amid Haley Stevens Reversal: 'He's a Fighter' Tate McRae's 'Housewife' Scores Second Week at No. 1 on Billboard Global Charts

The track’s resurgence can be traced to the Victoria’s Secret Fashion Show. During the Oct. 18 event in Los Angeles, which was streamed live, Kylie Jenner walked the runway to the song in a $50 million Fantasy Bra, a moment that quickly went viral across social media. Though Jade didn’t perform the song live, the synch resulted in a sizable streaming surge. As Billboard reported , “Angel of My Dreams” logged 18,000 official U.S. streams on the day of the show, then vaulted 1,434% to more than 284,000 the following day.

The song’s Hot 100 arrival follows its No. 6 debut on the Hot Dance /Pop Songs chart (dated Oct. 31), where it climbs to No. 4 in its second week.

Jade previously charted three songs on the Hot 100 as a member of Little Mix: “Wings” (No. 79 peak in 2013), “Black Magic” (No. 67, 2015) and “Shout Out to My Ex” (No. 69, 2016).

Little Mix formed on the U.K.’s The X Factor in 2011 and became the first group to win the competition. The quartet, comprising Jade (Thirlwall), Perrie Edwards, Jesy Nelson and Leigh-Anne Pinnock, first appeared on a U.S. Billboard chart in March 2013 when “Wings” debuted at No. 40 on the Pop Airplay chart, later peaking at No. 26. The act has logged five songs on Pop Airplay, plus two on Dance Airplay, including the No. 1 “Heartbreak Anthem,” with Galantis and David Guetta, in 2021.

Back home, the group was a much bigger force. Little Mix charted 25 songs on the U.K.’s Official Singles Chart in 2011-21, including five No. 1s: “Cannonball” (2011), “Wings” (2012), “Black Magic” (2015), “Shout Out to My Ex” (2016) and “Sweet Melody” (2021). Nelson left in December 2020 and the remaining trio went on hiatus in 2022.

entertainment.title: Paris Jackson Wants $600M From Michael’s Estate Put in Family Trust, Rips Executor’s ‘Iron Grip’
entertainment.summary: Michael Jackson's daughter has been battling with executor John Branca for more than a year over the attorney's continued control of her father's massive estate.
entertainment.body:
Michael Jackson ’s daughter Paris is now demanding that $600 million be released from her father’s estate to a family trust, accusing the estate’s executor of maintaining an “iron grip” over the late legend’s assets.

One day after attorneys for Paris sharply criticized estate executor John Branca’s compensation, she filed a new petition in Los Angeles court arguing that he has “done nothing” to fund a trust intended to benefit her and her brothers, Prince, 29, and Bigi, 24.

“Michael intended for his children to become the caretakers of his legacy,” lawyers for Paris write in the Oct. 29 filing, reviewed by Billboard . “Instead, Executor continues to keep each beneficiary beholden to him with an iron grip over when and if monies are distributed to them.”

The testy new filing, which says Paris is “uncowed by Executor’s intimidation tactics,” comes amid an ongoing feud with Branca, a prominent music attorney who has run the estate since Jackson’s sudden 2009 death. Branca has won plaudits for his well-documented financial success, but Paris has repeatedly attacked his continued control over her father’s estate, which remains stuck in probate court more than 17 years after his passing.

In a response statement to the new filing, the estate said Paris is “well aware” that the disputed trusts cannot be funded until the resolution of ongoing litigation with the IRS over the estate’s tax bill, a court battle that has been pending for years. Despite those limitations, the estate said, more than $200 million has already been distributed to her and her siblings.

“Michael Jackson’s will is clear,” the estate said in the statement. “None of his children receive a distribution until they are in their 30s. The Estate looks forward to the time when all issues are resolved so that their trusts can be fully funded as Michael wanted.”

The new court filing from Paris’ attorneys says the three siblings were supposed to start getting paid from the family trust on their 21 st birthdays. But instead, she says they get “lesser amounts” that are “dictated” by Branca, who “uses this power to deter them from checking his abuses.”

She says the estate sat on $850 million in cash in December 2024, and currently holds “approximately $600 million in distributable cash” even when various debts and other liabilities are taken into account. The filing seeks a court order forcing the estate to put that money in the family trust.

For his new album Mosca , Mexican musician Nsqk embraced the desire for greatness as his thesis while delving into the horrors of the modern world that Czech author Franz Kafka foreshadowed in his masterpiece The Metamorphosis , published 110 years ago. Explore Billboard See latest videos, charts and news

It was 2024, and Rodrigo Torres (his real name) had just moved in with his partner to an apartment in the northern city of Monterrey when, as he tells Billboard Español , an unexpected plague of flies invaded their home. Related Justin Timberlake to Release 4-Part Docuseries That Includes Janet Jackson as a Guest Bruce Springsteen Backs Michigan's Dr. Abdul El-Sayed for U.S. Senate Amid Haley Stevens Reversal: 'He's a Fighter' Tate McRae's 'Housewife' Scores Second Week at No. 1 on Billboard Global Charts

“There were flies, big, cemetery-like, very ugly ones, and at first I didn’t think much of it, until three, four, five started appearing each day. I began to get scared,” he recalls. “I felt like I was living in a horror movie. We weren’t messy people, and we couldn’t find an apparent reason for their presence.” So, at his manager’s suggestion, he agreed to see a shaman.

“The shaman told me that someone had done a spell on me, and that these types of witchcraft manifest as plagues,” he says. After a session with that man, Nsqk (pronounced like the chocolate powder brand) says he returned to his apartment, “and surprisingly, there were no flies anymore.”

With the plague gone, the musician entered a period of reflection. He says he compared the process artists go through when achieving fame to the transformation experienced by Kafka’s protagonist, Gregor Samsa. “It’s a metamorphosis,” he notes. “If it’s not controlled, it can become grotesque and unrecognizable.”

The changes Nsqk underwent during this time also led him to experience artistic evolution of new dimensions, making Mosca his most ambitious and accomplished album yet — one that promises to put him in the international spotlight by expanding his creative universe and challenging the boundaries of alternative music.

“I’m trying to bring other sounds to the table, more daring lyrics, and that stems from the fear of not meeting expectations, but transformed,” he explains about his new LP, released on Oct. 15. “As an artist, and with my team, we wanted to create something completely new, with the aim of not settling for what’s sufficient but always delivering quality.”

entertainment.title: ‘The Cat in the Hat’ Review: Bill Hader in a Dr. Seuss Adaptation That Captures the Antic Silliness but Misses the Charm
entertainment.summary: The voice cast also includes Quinta Brunson, Bowen Yang, America Ferrera, Giancarlo Esposito and Matt Berry.
entertainment.body:
About midway through the new animated adaptation of Dr. Seuss’ classic children’s book The Cat in the Hat , there’s an extended silent, slow-motion gag consisting of little more than a fish slowly swimming from one end of the wide screen to the other. It lasts for around 40 seconds and gets funnier as it goes along, with the lack of sound only adding to the mirth.

Take it in, because the wonderfully subtle sequence offers a much-needed respite from the otherwise unrelenting visual and narrative mayhem of the film, which captures the antic silliness of Dr. Seuss without the charm. There are some funny moments along the way, to be sure, of the necessarily juvenile kind (a lengthy bit involves confusion over the expressions “too far” and “toot fart”). Related Stories Beyond the Book 'The Cat in the Hat' Is Back: How the Seuss Icon's First Animated Feature Will Kick Off a New Era Movies Giancarlo Esposito and John Turturro Hated Each Other on 'Do the Right Thing.' Now They Break Character to Cry Mid-Scene The Cat in the Hat The Bottom Line Better than the live-action version, but not by much. Release date : Friday, November 6 Cast : Bill Hader, Mayabella Sage McCrilliss, Johnny Haemmerle, Quinta Brunson, Ryan Gaffney, Bowen Yang, Giancarlo Esposito, America Ferrera, Xochitl Gomez, Tiago Martinez, Asha Marie, Paula Pell, Matt Berry, Titus Burgess Directors-screenwriters : Erica Rivinoja, Alessandro Corloni Rated PG, 1 hour 47 minutes

But the film, while an improvement over the misbegotten 2003 live-action version starring Mike Myers, proves more taxing than enjoyable. It works well enough as a diverting animated effort geared to the youngest kids, and will eventually fulfill its role as streaming babysitter. But it could and should have been a whole lot more.

Bill Hader voices the title character and does as well as you would expect. But the true star of the voice cast turns out to be supporting player Matt Berry as pet goldfish Waffles, who observes the chaos around him with a hilariously droll, deadpan sophistication that produces the film’s biggest laughs even as he runs the risk of becoming a sushi meal.

More of a sequel to the original story than a true adaptation, the film, which begins with a frenetic musical number, presents the Cat not as an independent operator but rather a beleaguered employee of the “Institution of Imagination and Inspiration.” His latest assignment is to cheer up young siblings Gabby ( Xochitl Gomez , The Baby-Sitters Club ) and Sebastian (Tiago Martinez), whose single mother (an underused America Ferrera ) has just moved the family to a new town, much to their dismay.

entertainment.title: Tame Impala & JENNIE’s ‘Dracula’ Enters the Halloween Canon With Best Streaming Day Yet
entertainment.summary: The 2026 Hot 100 top five hit received an Oct. 31 bump of rare size for a relatively new song.
entertainment.body:
In many ways, the Halloween music canon is much like the one for Christmas music — once you’re in, you’re in forever, but it might take decades before you even get considered. Of the five songs that re-entered Billboard Hot 100 in 2025 as a result of a Halloween bump, the most recent was from 32 years earlier, with The Citizens of Halloween’s “This Is Halloween” from The Nightmare Before Christmas , with the other returns hailing from as far back as 1962 (Bobby “Boris” Pickett and the Crypt-Kickers’ “Monster Mash”). And a brand new (or even a relatively new) song becoming a Halloween staple is virtually unheard of. Related Justin Timberlake to Release 4-Part Docuseries That Includes Janet Jackson as a Guest Bruce Springsteen Backs Michigan's Dr. Abdul El-Sayed for U.S. Senate Amid Haley Stevens Reversal: 'He's a Fighter' Tate McRae's 'Housewife' Scores Second Week at No. 1 on Billboard Global Charts Explore Tame Impala See latest videos, charts and news

But this year, one contemporary hit is big enough and Halloween-y enough that it appears to be jumping the line, eschewing the usual waiting period for eligibility and declaring itself a holiday staple right away: Tame Impala & JENNIE’s “Dracula.”

The song, originally from Tame’s October 2025 album Deadbeat , has already grown into one of the biggest hits of 2026 — holding at its No. 5 high on the Hot 100 this week (dated Nov. 7) and spending the entire year thus far on the chart — with extra acceleration provided this year with its February-released official remix adding JENNIE. But even with the tremendous success it’s already achieved in the past year, Oct. 31 still marked another peak for “Dracula,” as it racked up 2.8 million official on-demand U.S. streams, according to Luminate — a new single-day high for the song, by a nearly 40% margin.

Previously, the best day for “Dracula” had come on April 6, when the song amassed just over 2 million streams — during the time when the JENNIE remix was really starting to go viral on TikTok, propelling the song to another level of pop success. The song’s 2.8 million streaming total from this Halloween also represented a 56% gain from the 1.8 million it racked up the prior Halloween, and a whopping 148% gain from the 1.1 million streams it posted the previous Saturday (Oct. 24).

It should be said that “Dracula” is not really a horror tale, so much as a delirious late-night lament of romantic longing. But with its horror-themed title, haunted-house synths and eerie wordless vocal hook, it still makes for a natural fit on spooky-season playlists.

When i was coming up people saw my skin last. They saw my teeth first.. the acne on my forehead.. my dusty braids and they called me a dirty stripper.”

“The reason why dark-skinned girls don’t get the same brand deals is because she’s light-skinned and she’s Dominican,” Love said in a recent video . “I don’t care if she considers herself a n— or not. You’re still Dominican, which is some type of fancy on it in this country.”

entertainment.title: ‘Starlog’ Magazine Returns with First Cover in 17 Years
entertainment.summary: The publication, once a fixture of geek culture, will relaunch as an annual offering.
entertainment.body:
Logo text The last time there was a new edition of Starlog magazine, J.J. Abrams’ Star Trek was still weeks away from hitting theaters, Robert Downey Jr. was just scratching the surface of Tony Stark’s potential on the set of Iron Man 2 , and George Lucas was still years away from selling Lucasfilm to Disney.

But 17 years after publishing its final issue in April 2009, Starlog is back with a new edition, which arrives Nov. 13.

The magazine launched in 1976 and gained a fanbase for being one of the few places to get reliable news and interviews about geek culture. It launched with a cover focusing on Star Trek , one of its key areas of expertise, but the magazine’s editors and writers also pioneered coverage of Star Wars . (The new issue chronicles some of the rumors it put out a year before the movie opened). In all, Starlog published 374 issues and more than 25,000 pages. Related Stories Lifestyle GQ Expands Men of the Year Footprint in L.A. Movies Cinemark Won't Screen Brad Pitt's 'Cliff Booth' Movie Over Netflix's Demands, CEO Says

The new iteration will publish one issue a year under editor in chief Annalee Newitz, a founding editor of io9 . In addition to the film and TV-focused features Starlog was known for, the new Starlog will also delve into futurism, as the cover from Gabriel Yeganyan highlights. The opening story of issue No. 1 looks at the viability of humans farming crops on planets outside of Earth, for example.

“Science fiction and fantasy give us a sandbox to reimagine our world, and Starlog is your invitation to play along,” said Newitz in a statement. “We’re honoring the fannish legacy of the original magazine and bringing it into the future with hopeful, awe-inspiring, and scientifically grounded explorations of where humanity could go next.”

“During its original 33-year run, Starlog documented science fiction as it evolved across film, television, books, technology, and culture,” said co-owner Tara Ansley. “Fifty years after the magazine first launched, the line between science fiction and the real world has become increasingly difficult to separate. That makes this an especially interesting time to bring Starlog back. Technology may change, but the most compelling questions have always been about people: how we live, what we create, and what kind of future we want to build.”

entertainment.title: Offset Reveals New Release Date for Upcoming Album ‘GMFU’: ‘For Too Long I Let People Speak on My Name’
entertainment.summary: The project was originally slated to arrive in October.
entertainment.body:
Offset has had enough of the chatter, and it’s time to clear his name of the misconceptions and rumors flooding social media. Essentially, y’all have had him “f—ked up.” The Migos rapper announced on Monday (Nov. 2) that his upcoming album, GMFU (short for Got Me F—ked Up ), has a new release date set for Nov. 13.

“Got me f–ked up. For too long I let people speak on my name like they know what it took to get here. I came from nothing to something,” he wrote in a caption to IG that feels more like a rapped verse. “I made history. I lost people. I lost myself at times but always found my way back. I ain’t perfect. Never claimed to be. I made mistakes. I made choices I had to live with. And I can own that.”

Set continued to wear his flaws: “But everything I got, I had to fight for. And everything I’ve been through made me who I am today. I’m not asking for respect. I earned that. I’m not asking to be understood. Just hear me. GMFU. THE ALBUM. 11/13.”

The 35-year-old also shared the project’s cover art, which shows him in camouflage pants and an American flag over his head, with eye black on, sitting on a stoop alongside a foursome of ballet dancers.

Offset is sounding more motivated in the booth, as he teased an unreleased snippet over the weekend, rapping over triumphant production courtesy of FnZ and Jaasu. “I came to pop my s–t,” he wrote.

The Atlanta native kicked off his latest solo era with “Something I Need” in September and returned in October with the Jodeci -sampling “Every Night,” which features an appearance from Don Toliver.

In between Set’s singles, he also reunited with his Migos running mate, Quavo, for “Away,” which landed on Huncho’s album QROMELIFE . Fans can expect the reunion to continue as Quavo and Offset are slated to lock in for a final Migos project in 2027.

GMFU serves as Offset’s first solo album since Kiari , which arrived in August 2025 and peaked at No. 16 on the Billboard 200.

entertainment.title: GQ Expands Men of the Year Footprint in L.A.
entertainment.summary: GQ drafted cover stars Chris Rock, Andrew Garfield and Matt Damon as Men of the Year co-hosts.
entertainment.body:
GQ ‘s Men of the Year footprint in Los Angeles is growing — with some A-list names in tow.

A marquee franchise for the Condé Nast publication, Men of the Year will be celebrated at three events this month in a showing that will mark the mag’s most ambitious run in the annual rollout. And this time it’s being steered by global editorial director Adam Baidawi, who took over in February 2026 after longtime editor Will Welch departed for a role working for Pharrell Williams in Paris.

GQ has drafted Chris Rock , Andrew Garfield and Matt Damon to serve as Men of the Year co-hosts for their respective work in Misty Green, Artificial and The Odyssey . The three cover stars will bring some star power to the 31st installment of the series, which will also feature fellow honorees like GQ’s director of the year Denis Villeneuve for Dune: Part Three and designer of the year Michael Rider of Celine. Related Stories Music Tom Morello, Annie Lennox, 'KPop Demon Hunters' Songwriters Honored at 2026 SONA Awards Lifestyle Bob Iger Stresses Value of Communal Cultural Experiences in World "Rife With Disruption and Polarization" at PAC NYC Icons of Culture Gala

As for those events, the Men of the Year celebration kicks off Nov. 10 at the recently opened Lucas Museum of Narrative Art, where GQ will host Villeneuve with a champagne reception, a live recording of GQ’s “One More Question” interview series fronted by senior special projects editor Zach Baron and a VIP screening of Dune: Part Two ahead of the franchise’s final bow on Dec. 18.

Next up will be a “Breakouts” house party at the Sheats-Goldstein Residence on Nov. 11. The soiree wil host and toast the mag’s 13 Breakouts of 2026, a roster of boldfaced names across film, TV, music, comedy and podcasting. (The list will be published on GQ.com on Nov. 9.)

And last but not least: the anticipated Men of the Year bash will return to Chateau Marmont on Nov. 12. An intimate dinner honoring the GQ’s cover stars will open the night and feature some starry (and filmed) toasts from special guests who will fete their friends. Then, after dessert, the action turns up a notch for the annual Men of the Year party that will once again host VIPs across entertainment, fashion, sports and culture.

“This year’s GQ Men of the Year honorees have delivered extraordinary performances and propelled the cultural conversation of 2026. We wanted to meet that creative ambition with some of our own. Expanding to three events in Los Angeles — something brand new to Men of the Year — gives us the space to celebrate their work, get into the ideas behind it and introduce the talent we think everyone needs to watch next. It’s an ambitious new chapter for a tradition we love,” Baidawi tells The Hollywood Reporter in a statement.

entertainment.title: Cinemark Won’t Screen Brad Pitt’s ‘Cliff Booth’ Movie Over Netflix’s Demands, CEO Says
entertainment.summary: Cinemark boss says agreeing to the streamer's ultra-short two-week release window is "not aligned [with] what's of the greatest interest in our theaters."
entertainment.body:
Two theater chains are refusing to screen the upcoming sequel to Once Upon a Time… in Hollywood .

Cinemark and Regal have decided against giving any of their Imax screens to The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth , which has Brad Pitt reprising his role as a fearless stuntman in a movie written by Quentin Tarantino and directed by David Fincher. The decision effectively makes Cliff Booth exclusive to AMC among the major chains.

During Cinemark’s third-quarter earnings call early Tuesday, CEO Sean Gamble explained that the company decided against running the film due to Netflix ‘s very short release window — which ends just two weeks before the title shifts to streaming — and not wanting to establish a precedent that could come back to haunt the chain in future negotiations.

“The Cliff Booth situation is an interesting one,” Gamble said. “We book all of our films on a case-by-case situation. In that particular situation, we always look at things through a long-term lens and how certain precedents and things we might do could affect longer-term industry dynamics. In this particular case, we don’t believe the proposed release model is constructive for the broader theatrical ecosystem, and it’s not aligned [with] what’s of the greatest interest in our theaters.” Gamble also added that keeping The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping on its Imax screens during Thanksgiving is a sold play due to the film’s strong advance sales.

Cliff Booth will debut in theaters on Nov. 25, then hit Netflix on Dec. 23.

For Netflix, which has traditionally resisted filmmakers’ efforts to secure theatrical releases for their movies, the film actually represents a first — the first time the streamer has released a movie in Imax. The slot was originally supposed to go to Greta Gerwig’s Narnia: The Magician’s Nephew , but the movie was pushed to February, where it will have a far more generous seven-week theatrical window.

Cinemark Holdings posted higher revenue and earnings compared to a year ago, seeing total revenue rise to $1.05 billion versus $857.5 million in the same period of 2025. Gamble predicted the theatrical window could actually widen despite the rise of streaming.

“We’re going to continue to see [the window] grow, especially since the commitments were a minimum of 45 days and beyond that many of the larger films continue to have windows of 60-plus days,” he said. “As we turn the corner into 2027, we’re going to see that window continue to expand a bit, especially as additional studios join in.”

entertainment.title: Josh O’Connor Calls Bond Speculation “Incredibly Bizarre Pinch Me Moment”
entertainment.summary: The 'Disclosure Day' actor has also weighed in on the reports that he, Callum Turner and Jack Lowden are in the running to replace Daniel Craig.
entertainment.body:
Logo text Josh O’Connor is the latest star to play coy on the reports — including those from The Hollywood Reporter — that he is in the running for the role of James Bond .

The Crown , Knives Out and Challengers actor was said to be screen-testing to replace Daniel Craig as Ian Fleming’s iconic MI6 agent. Among the small group of actors also in contention are Callum Turner and Jack Lowden . The Scottish Slow Horses star weighed in just this week on the speculation , telling British GQ : “Oh, Christ… It’s all very flattering. It’s nice to be mentioned — for any role — and I’m just not really going to add to the noise.” Related Stories Movies Pierce Brosnan Supports Callum Turner Being Cast as James Bond: "So Strong..." General News British Celebrity Loses Legal Bid to Prevent Publication of Identity and Sexual Misconduct Allegations

The 36-year-old O’Connor, who also led Steven Spielberg’s Disclosure Day earlier this year, was opening the new Everyman Theatre in his hometown of Cheltenham, England, on Tuesday. He was probed about the Bond reports and admitted: “To be considered in that same sort of bracket is extraordinary.”

He described the news as “such an incredibly bizarre pinch me moment… even being uttered in that same sentence and being considered for something like that. But I am afraid,” he continued, “there is nothing to say beyond that.”

Toward the end of October, THR heard word that screen tests for Amazon MGM Studios’ James Bond film, directed by Dune ‘s Denis Villeneuve and written by Peaky Blinders mastermind Steven Knight, would be taking place in London imminently.

While Jack O’Connell, star of Sinners and 28 Years Later: The Bone Temple , was rumored to be in the mix, sources confirmed this is not the case. Euphoria alum Jacob Elordi is also not testing.

Also on Friday, in a new interview with Vanity Fair , former Bond himself Pierce Brosnan weighed in on the debate . “Oh, I’m just an audience member now,” he said. “I’m just the man in the street who is eager to see who is going to play this epic role of cinematic history.”

The MobLand actor did say he admired all of the actors on the proposed list, but shouted out his Only Living Boy in New York co-star in particular. “Callum Turner is someone I’ve worked with, and he’s so strong,” said Brosnan. “They all have a voice and a physique, and a presence on film. They all have longevity as actors, all of these young men. Whoever plays the role, I wish him the very best of life and strength and courage. You know, it’s hard to tell who it would be, but I eagerly await to hear the news and the celebration of the next James Bond.”

entertainment.title: Pierce Brosnan Supports Callum Turner Being Cast as James Bond: “So Strong…”
entertainment.summary: The 007 star weighed in on the actors in contention for the iconic role and director Denis Villeneuve taking over the franchise.
entertainment.body:
Logo text Former James Bond star Pierce Brosnan gave an enthusiastic shout-out to Callum Turner in his quest to become the next 007.

During an interview with Vanity Fair , Brosnan was asked about the current “conversation” around the subject of Bond — presumably referring to media coverage about the actors reportedly being tested to take over the iconic role.

The MobLand actor was very diplomatic in his answer, generously praising the field of young stars who are up for the part. Related Stories Movies Jack Lowden Is Tight-Lipped on Those Bond Rumors: "I'm Not Going to Add to the Noise" Movies Lowden, Turner or a Dark Horse: One James Bond Casting Test Has Nothing to Do With Acting

Yet he did give a particular hat tip to Turner, whom he worked with on the 2017 film The Only Living Boy in New York .

“Oh, I’m just an audience member now,” he said. “I’m just the man in the street who is eager to see who is going to play this epic role of cinematic history. All the men who are on the list now are actors I admire. Callum Turner is someone I’ve worked with, and he’s so strong. They all have a voice and a physique, and a presence on film. They all have longevity as actors, all of these young men. Whoever plays the role, I wish him the very best of life and strength and courage. You know, it’s hard to tell who it would be, but I eagerly await to hear the news and the celebration of the next James Bond.”

Brosnan also had praise for Dune director Denis Villeneuve helming the new Bond film.

“I think we are going to be blown away,” he said. “[Villeneuve] is such an iconoclastic director. His work is visionary, and his stealth and imagination of camera work and storytelling is so visceral and sensuous. It’s going to be great. It’s going to be truly magnificent.”

As reported by The Hollywood Reporter , the actors testing for Bond include Turner and Slow Horses star Jack Lowden. Going into last weekend when auditions were set to take place, Lowden was the favorite in prediction markets. Since then, for whatever reason, Turner has surged ahead.

entertainment.title: British Celebrity Loses Legal Bid to Prevent Publication of Identity and Sexual Misconduct Allegations
entertainment.summary: The unnamed man will, however, remain anonymous during the period allowed for his appeal.
entertainment.body:
Logo text A judge has ruled that an unnamed British celebrity facing allegations of “inappropriate sexual activities with a large number of girls and young women” can be named in the press, but will remain anonymous while an appeal is lodged.

The man had sought an injunction to prevent two news organisations, ITN and Guardian News and Media, from publishing his identity, over fears that he would be “highly likely” to kill himself. He maintained that the suicide risk is not attributed to any wrongdoing but because of what his lawyers described as “trial by media.” Related Stories Business Tokyo: Industry Insiders Skeptical of Bold Japanese Government Plans for Overseas Content Sales Push Business Tokyo: Japan's New Production Incentives Risk Doing as Much Harm as Good

In a judgment that came Tuesday, Justice Nicklin rejected the injunction request and said: “The court did not determine whether the allegations, or any of them, were true, and the dismissal of the claim does not amount to approval of any publication the defendants may decide to make.”

According to BBC News , London’s High Court heard that the celebrity denies that he abused “his power and position as a celebrity to contact and forge relationships with young women and teenagers to try to have sex with them.”

Lawyers for ITN and the Guardian said his suicide risk could be mitigated and that there was no basis “to restrain the publication of public interest journalism.”

Justice Nicklin had previously said there was “significant public interest” in the proceedings and that “this is a difficult and important case… The court must determine it fairly, on the evidence and legal submissions.”

The British press have been warned against publishing any details that could identify the celebrity.

Sara Mansoori, the lawyer representing the celebrity, told the judge in written submissions: “This is not a case where an individual has spuriously raised ‘mental health’ concerns in the face of an impending publication that they do not wish to occur… The claimant has attempted suicide twice as a result of these matters, been hospitalised for months, been the subject of involuntary detention and been examined by multiple — now more than 10 — doctors.”

entertainment.title: Sony Partners With Lionsgate on Destin Daniel Cretton’s ‘Naruto’ Movie (Exclusive)
entertainment.summary: The live-action adaptation of the popular manga has been greenlit to start production in spring 2027.
entertainment.body:
Logo text Lionsgate has partnered with Sony Pictures for its high-profile feature adaptation of Naruto .

The deal, which came after competitive, multi-studio bidding, will see Sony co-finance the movie and take on international distribution of the live-action feature film that is based on the manga by Masashi Kishimoto that grew into a global entertainment brand.

Lionsgate has now officially greenlit the project, which is the follow-up feature for Destin Daniel Cretton , who his coming off the $2.5 billion success of Spider-Man: Brand New Day . Cretton is writing the script and will direct and produce. Production slated to begin in spring 2027, with Lionsgate continuing to oversee the film’s development and production and handle domestic distribution. Related Stories Business Lionsgate Inks Deal With Meta to Bring New 'Hunger Games' Movie to VR Glasses Movies 'The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping' First Reactions

That Sony’s motion picture group, headed by Tom Rothman, would come out on top seems almost pre-ordained. Cretton in September signed a three-year first-look producing deal with the studio, signaling a strong relationship with his Brand New Day partner. And Sony, which is headquartered in Japan, is also the home of Crunchyroll, the popular and arguably largest streaming service that focuses on anime.

“With their deep expertise in manga and anime and global distribution prowess, Sony Pictures is a perfect partner for Naruto , and we’re thrilled to join forces with Tom Rothman and his team to bring this extraordinary property to audiences around the world,” said Lionsgate Motion Picture Group chair Adam Fogelson in a statement. “We share an enormous ambition for Naruto and a commitment to making this a truly global cinematic event that stays true to what millions of existing fans love and invites so many more to embrace what makes it truly special.

Fogelson added, “I’m tremendously proud of Erin Westerman and James Myers for their work developing this film and bringing Destin aboard, and of Helen Lee-Kim for securing Sony as our international partner. Ari Arad, Tetsu Fujimura, and our producing team also deserve huge thanks for their hard work and support.”

Stated Rothman, Sony’s Motion Picture Group CEO and chairman, “Lionsgate has done a masterful job in putting together an A-level adaptation, and we are honored to be chosen as their partner. Not to mention, we had a sweet success this summer with Destin and are delighted to be back in his capable hands.”
